blocks.text: Imagine flipping a fair coin multiple times and counting the number of heads. How can we model this probabilistically?

blocks.markdown: In probability theory, certain distributions help us model scenarios involving repeated trials and waiting times. In this lesson, we will explore the Bernoulli, Binomial, and Geometric distributions. These distributions are fundamental for modeling binary outcomes and waiting times in repeated experiments.

blocks.title: Bernoulli Distribution
blocks.text: A Bernoulli distribution models a single trial with two possible outcomes: success (with probability $p$) and failure (with probability $1-p$).

blocks.markdown: The Bernoulli distribution is the simplest discrete distribution. It is the building block for more complex distributions like the Binomial distribution.

blocks.title: Binomial Distribution
blocks.text: A Binomial distribution models the number of successes in $n$ independent Bernoulli trials, each with success probability $p$.

blocks.caption: Probability mass function of the Binomial distribution

blocks.title: Computing Binomial Probabilities
blocks.prompt: A fair coin is flipped 5 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 3 heads?

steps.text: Use the Binomial probability mass function.
Calculate the binomial coefficient and probabilities.

blocks.answer: The probability of getting exactly 3 heads is 0.3125.

blocks.title: Geometric Distribution
blocks.text: A Geometric distribution models the number of trials until the first success in a series of independent Bernoulli trials, each with success probability $p$.

blocks.caption: Probability mass function of the Geometric distribution

blocks.title: Modeling Waiting Times with Geometric Distribution
blocks.prompt: A die is rolled repeatedly until a 6 appears. What is the probability that the first 6 appears on the 4th roll?

steps.text: Use the Geometric probability mass function.

blocks.answer: The probability that the first 6 appears on the 4th roll is approximately 0.0964.

blocks.title: Mean and Variance
blocks.text: For a Binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$, the mean is $np$ and the variance is $np(1-p)$. For a Geometric distribution with parameter $p$, the mean is $\frac{1}{p}$ and the variance is $\frac{1-p}{p^2}$.

points: The Bernoulli distribution models a single trial with two outcomes.
The Binomial distribution models the number of successes in multiple trials.
The Geometric distribution models the waiting time for the first success.
